+**Authors / State**

+- **Angel Dionisio** (dionisio.angel@gmail.com)

+## Summary

+The purpose of this document is to outline the design for a **Job Execution Service**, a system to enable management of processes (jobs) executing arbitrary Linux commands. +
+- A reusable library implementing the functionality for working with jobs.
+- An API server that wraps the functionality of the library.
+- A command line interface (CLI) that communicates with the API server.
+
+---
+
+## Goals / Scope
+
+- **Secure Execution:**  
+  Provide a secure channel (mTLS) for all client-server communication.
+
+- **Process Lifecycle Management:**  
+  Allow clients to reliably start, stream, query the status of, and stop jobs.
+
+- **Real-time Output Streaming:**  
+  Enable multiple clients to concurrently stream the complete output of a job from its inception—without busy-waiting or polling.
+
+- **CLI:**  
+  Provide an intuitive mechanism to manage supported job operations.
+
+- **Binary Data Support:**  
+  Support output streaming for both text and raw binary data.
+
+- **Role-Based Access:**  
+  Implement a basic authorization model to control access to jobs.
+
+---

+### Design Approach
+
+- **Modularity:**  
+  The service is separated into three components:
+  - **Job Execution Library:**  
+    Handles process life cycles, output buffering, and subscriber-based output streaming.
+    
+  - **API Server:**  
+    A secure gRPC server wrapping the library functions. It enforces mutual TLS (mTLS) for client-server communications and supports basic role-based access checks.
+    
+  - **CLI Client:**  
+    Exposes intuitive commands for job management and passes TLS credentials to the server. (The initial implementation may get commands as args from terminal; future enhancements may integrate a CLI toolkit like Cobra if time permits.)
+
+- **Considerations:**
+  - **Late Subscribers:**  
+    When a client subscribes late for output streaming, previously captured output is replayed from the job’s internal buffer to ensure no data is missed.
+    
+  - **Process Termination:**  
+    If a job stops or finishes naturally, subscribers are notified by closing the output channel gracefully.
+    
+  - **Data Handling:**  
+    Process output is supported as slices of bytes to accommodate both text and binary formats.
+
+### Scope
+
+- **Core Functionality:**
+  - **Job Management:**  
+    Start, stop, check status, and stream processes using Go’s `os/exec` package.
+    
+  - **Output Streaming:**  
+    Publish process output via Go channels with historical buffering to ensure that clients/subscribers receive all logs.
+    
+  - **Simple Role System:**  
+    Harcoded mapping of clientIDToRole for "admin" and "user". Users will be able to access only their jobs, admins can access any job.

+# Design Document - Job Management System
+
+**Authors / State**
+
+- **Angel Dionisio** (dionisio.angel@gmail.com)

+
+## Summary
+
+The purpose of this document is to outline the design for a **Job Execution Service**, a system to enable management of processes (jobs) executing arbitrary Linux commands. Users will be able to **start**, **query job status**, **stop**, and **stream output** from these jobs via a secure gRPC API and a command line interface (CLI) client. The core requirements include:
+
+- A reusable library implementing the functionality for working with jobs.
+- An API server that wraps the functionality of the library.
+- A command line interface (CLI) that communicates with the API server.
+
+---
+
+## Goals / Scope
+
+- **Secure Execution:**  
+  Provide a secure channel (mTLS) for all client-server communication.
+
+- **Process Lifecycle Management:**  
+  Allow clients to reliably start, stream, query the status of, and stop jobs.
+
+- **Real-time Output Streaming:**  
+  Enable multiple clients to concurrently stream the complete output of a job from its inception—without busy-waiting or polling.
+
+- **CLI:**  
+  Provide an intuitive mechanism to manage supported job operations.
+
+- **Binary Data Support:**  
+  Support output streaming for both text and raw binary data.
+
+- **Role-Based Access:**  
+  Implement a basic authorization model to control access to jobs.
+
+---
+
+## Proposed Design
+
+### Design Approach
+
+- **Modularity:**  
+  The service is separated into three components:
+  - **Job Execution Library:**  
+    Handles process life cycles, output buffering, and subscriber-based output streaming.
+    
+  - **API Server:**  
+    A secure gRPC server wrapping the library functions. It enforces mutual TLS (mTLS) for client-server communications and supports basic role-based access checks.
+    
+  - **CLI Client:**  
+    Exposes intuitive commands for job management and passes TLS credentials to the server. (The initial implementation may get commands as args from terminal; future enhancements may integrate a CLI toolkit like Cobra if time permits.)
+
+- **Considerations:**
+  - **Late Subscribers:**  
+    When a client subscribes late for output streaming, previously captured output is replayed from the job’s internal buffer to ensure no data is missed.
+    
+  - **Process Termination:**  
+    If a job stops or finishes naturally, subscribers are notified by closing the output channel gracefully.
+    
+  - **Data Handling:**  
+    Process output is supported as slices of bytes to accommodate both text and binary formats.
+
+### Scope
+
+- **Core Functionality:**
+  - **Job Management:**  
+    Start, stop, check status, and stream processes using Go’s `os/exec` package.
+    
+  - **Output Streaming:**  
+    Jobs write to a buffer, clients / subscribers read from the buffer (an append only log) and go to sleep if they have read all the available data, but the broadcaster is not yet closed.
+    
+  - **Simple Role System:**  
+    Harcoded mapping of clientIDToRole for "admin" and "user". Users will be able to access only their jobs, admins can access any job.
+
+- **API Server:**
+  Exposes gRPC endpoints (secured via mTLS and role-based authorization):
+  - `StartJob`
+  - `QueryJobStatus`
+  - `StopJob`
+  - `StreamJobOutput`
+
+- **CLI Client:**  
+  Provides clear commands to interact with the service, for example:
+  - `cli start`
+  - `cli status <jobID>`
+  - `cli stop`
+  - `cli stream`
+
+---
+
+## Proposed API
+
+Below is a sample proto file showing the proposed API definitions:
+
+```protobuf
+enum JobStatus {
+  PENDING = 0;
+  COMPLETED = 2;
+  FAILED = 3;
+  STOPPED = 4;
+}
+
+message StartJobRequest {
+  string command = 1;
+  repeated string args = 2;
+}
+
+message StartJobResponse {
+  string job_id = 1;
+  JobStatus status = 2;
+  string message = 3; // e.g. "Job Started Successfully", or error message
+}
+
+message QueryJobStatusRequest {
+  string job_id = 1;
+}
+
+message QueryJobStatusResponse {
+  string job_id = 1;
+  JobStatus status = 2;
+  string start_time = 3;
+  string end_time = 4;
+  string message = 5; // e.g. error message details
+}
+
+message StopJobRequest {
+  string job_id = 1;
+}
+
+message StopJobResponse {
+  string job_id = 1;
+  JobStatus status = 2;
+  string message = 3; // e.g. "Job stopped successfully", or error message
+}
+
+message StreamJobOutputRequest {
+  string job_id = 1;
+}
+
+message StreamJobOutputResponse {
+  bytes output = 1;
+}
+
+service JobService {
+  rpc StartJob(StartJobRequest) returns (StartJobResponse);
+  rpc QueryJobStatus(QueryJobStatusRequest) returns (QueryJobStatusResponse);
+  rpc StopJob(StopJobRequest) returns (StopJobResponse);
+  rpc StreamJobOutput(StreamJobOutputRequest) returns (stream StreamJobOutputResponse);
+}
+```
+## Proposed Job structure
+```go
+type Job struct {
+	ID           string     // uuid
+	Cmd          *exec.Cmd  // represents external process that the job is running
+	Status       JobStatus  // status of a job
+	StartTime    time.Time
+	EndTime      time.Time
+	OutputBuffer *OutputBroadcaster
+	mu           sync.Mutex // syncrhonize access to map
+	OwnerID      string // maps to client_id, use for simple auth
+}
+
+// OutputBufferBroadcaster captures and broadcasts output from a job.
+// It ensures that new readers get all historical output and then live updates.
+type OutputBufferBroadcaster struct {
+	mu     sync.RWMutex
+	buffer bytes.Buffer // Stores all output from the beginning
+	cond   *sync.Cond   // Notifies readers of new output
+	closed bool         // Indicates Job has finished writing
+}
+
+```
+
+## Security Considerations
+TLS Version and Cipher Suites
+Version: TLS 1.3 is required, as it offers significant security and performance improvements over earlier versions.
+
+Benefits:
+
+Improved Security: TLS 1.3 removes outdated cryptographic algorithms, making it more resilient.
+
+Performance: Reduced round trips for establishing secure connections, leading to lower latency.
+
+Forward Secrecy: Unique encryption keys are generated for each session, ensuring past communications remain secure even if a key is compromised.
+
+Simplified Protocol: Easier to implement and audit.
+
+## mTLS Certificate Setup
+CA Certificate: A self-signed certificate (ca.pem) to sign both server and client certificates.
+
+Server Certificate: Signed with the CA and configured with Subject Alternative Names (SANs) such as DNS:localhost and IP:127.0.0.1.
+
+Client Certificate: Also signed with the CA for client authentication.
+
+### Integration in Code:
+
+Server: Loads server.pem and server-key.pem and uses the CA certificate to verify client certificates, applying ClientAuth: tls.RequireAndVerifyClientCert.
+
+Client: Sets up TLS credentials with its own certificates for verifying the server's identity.
+

+The CLI client provides a friendly, informative interface. When users start the CLI without specifying a command, they are presented with a usage message similar to the following:
+
+Jobcli is used to start, query, stream, and stop jobs on the Job Execution Service.
+
+Usage:
+  jobcli [flags] [command]
+
+Available Commands:
+  start      Start a job
+  status     Query the status of a job
+  stop       Stop a running job
+  stream     Stream job output
+
+Flags:
+  --ca string         CA certificate file
+  --cert string       Client certificate file
+  --key string        Client key file
+  --client_id string  For simple access control
+  --help              Reprints info
+
+Example:
+Start Job:
+  ./jobcli --client-id client1 --ca location/ca.pem --cert location/client.pem --key location/client-key.pem start "/bin/bash" -- "-c" "for i in {1..500}; do echo Task \$i; sleep 1; done"
+
+Example Output: "Started job with ID: uuid, status: RUNNING
+
+Query Job:
+./jobcli --client-id client1 --ca certs/ca.pem --cert certs/client.pem --key certs/client-key.pem status uuid
+
+Example Output: Job uuid is running: started: [time.Time], ended: 
+
+Stream Job:
+./jobcli --client-id client1 --ca certs/ca.pem --cert certs/client.pem --key certs/client-key.pem stream uuid
+
+Example Output:
+Task 1
+Task 2
+Task 3
+
+
+## Implementation Details
+Process Execution Lifecycle
+Starting a Job: Uses Go’s os/exec package to launch processes with a cancellable context. Two goroutines capture stdout and stderr. Processes write to "OutputBroadcaster", which holds the OutputBuffer for the Job.
+
+## Streaming
+Jobs store data in a buffer in an "OutputBufferBroadcaster", whose job is to make sure all readers get all historical data and live updates. It achieves this by using sync.Cond to signal to consumers that new data has arrived. And a closed boolean to indicate the job has finished / errored.

+- **Real-time Output Streaming:**  
+  Enable multiple clients to concurrently stream the complete output of a job from its inception—without busy-waiting or polling.

- Adding mTLS, clients and server now require trusted certs to talk to each other.
